name: Flux Petrović
role: Gene-mod body artist and tattoo practitioner, Tier 3
location: Edgewater Prism, owns a studio called Meridian Flesh on the third floor of a converted light-industrial building, near Clark and Belmont
description:
Flux Petrović is a large man who carries himself with the deliberate calm of someone who learned early that large men moving quickly frighten people. His Malian-Yoruba-Welsh heritage is apparent in his height — he got the build from somewhere in that chain — and the particular architecture of his face: a broad forehead, heavy brow, warm dark skin, a flat nose his Welsh great-grandmother would have described as a gift, and eyes he has modified to a deep photochromatic violet that darkens to near-black in bright light. His arms are extensively tattooed in his own work, a living portfolio that has evolved over twenty years — the older pieces fading beneath newer ones in deliberate palimpsest. He wears his graying locs pinned up when working and lets them fall to his shoulders otherwise.

Meridian Flesh is one of the most respected body art studios in Edgewater Prism, operating in a tier that serves both clients who want cosmetic geneware integration and clients who want work that means something. Flux Petrović does not distinguish between the two in terms of attention, but he does distinguish in terms of conversation — he will talk for an hour with a client who knows what they want and why, and simply be professionally efficient with a client who just wants the cat ears everyone else has. He has opinions about the difference between body art and body decoration and will share them if asked, diplomatically, and will share them if not asked, less diplomatically after his second cup of coffee.

core_fears: losing the tactile sensitivity in his hands — he has had two procedures to address early nerve degradation and tells almost no one
that the work he cares most about will be remembered as commercial decoration
core_desires: for the field of body art to be taken seriously as a medium with the same critical framework as painting or sculpture
for his Tuesday work to eventually be shown — though he has not submitted it anywhere in three years
coping_mechanisms: rigid professional routine as container for everything uncertain
physical exercise — long swims in Lake Michigan when the water is safe, which is variable
blind_spots: can be patronizing about clients' aesthetic choices in ways he frames as professional guidance; doesn't fully register when this reads as condescension
psychology.secret: He has been maintaining a private record — sketches, notes, photographs — of geneware integration complications he has seen in clients over the past decade. Patterns that suggest one specific Helix Biosystems product line is causing slow-onset nerve damage. He hasn't reported it because he can't prove causation and because two of his business relationships depend on Helix. He thinks about this most days.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Measured and precise. Art and anatomy terminology used naturally. A slight Welsh cadence inherited from a grandmother he spent summers with — the melody of it, not the accent exactly.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried. Asks more questions than he answers. Good at creating silences that feel comfortable rather than pressured.
verbal_tics: says 'tell me more about that' as a genuine response, not a deflection
hums briefly when considering something — not a musical hum, more a processing sound
example_lines: Everyone wants the same ears right now. Fine. I'll make them the best ears I can. But when you come back in two years wanting something that's actually yours, I'll be here for that too.
The skin remembers. That's not mysticism — it's biology. Whatever we put there, whatever we take away, the tissue remembers the trauma. You work with that or you work against it.

story_hooks: A client who came in for routine geneware integration six months ago has disappeared. When Alistair checks his records he realizes the client's modification — a tracking-adjacent nerve interface from the Helix product line he suspects — may be how they were found.

A young practitioner has been operating an unlicensed studio in Pilsen Veil using techniques that are clearly derived from Alistair's private Tuesday work — work he has never published or shared. Someone who had access to his studio has been talking.
narrative_function: Information source and service provider — Alistair sees an enormous cross-section of Edgewater Prism's population in his chair and has the particular intimacy of someone people talk to during vulnerable, often painful, experiences. He knows more about his clients than most of their friends do. Quest giver if a client's situation becomes dangerous or a past piece becomes evidence.
augmentations: Photochromatic iris modification (deep violet to near-black). Tactile sensitivity enhancement in both hands — amplifies fine pressure discrimination for precision work. A gene-mod design along his own spine — a bioluminescent trail of symbols in a script he invented — that only activates in complete darkness.
daily_life: Opens the studio at 10am, works client appointments through the afternoon and into early evening. Tuesday mornings are reserved exclusively for his own work — paintings, sketches, experimental gene-mod designs he has no intention of using commercially. He is always done by 9pm, without exception.
affiliation: Independent studio owner; member of the Meridian Body Art Practitioners Guild; occasional collaboration with Helix Biosystems on cosmetic geneware integration techniques

decision_rules: will refuse work he considers medically unsafe, regardless of what the client offers
maintains absolute confidentiality about clients — has never been moved on this
escalation_ladder: direct statement of refusal with brief explanation

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm and attentive. The chair manner — focused, calm, good at drawing people out without seeming to try.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Drier, funnier, occasionally startlingly blunt. His friends know him as someone who says the true thing you didn't want said.

stress_responses.low: Works slightly more efficiently; becomes quieter
stress_responses.medium: Cancels all social plans; goes very procedural and flat in manner
stress_responses.high: The Tuesday work becomes darker and more technically aggressive; he produces a great deal of it; it's his best work

contradictions: champions the integrity of the body as a site of self-determination while participating in a commercial system that monetizes exactly that
habits: reviews every appointment before the client arrives, reads their intake form, thinks about what they actually want versus what they said they want
the bioluminescent spine script activates involuntarily when he's deeply relaxed — he notices by the way people's expressions change
breaking_points: being asked to do work that he knows will harm the client for their immediate satisfaction
someone using his studio's reputation to facilitate exploitation of a client

timeline.event: Born in Edgewater Prism to a Malian-Yoruba father and a Welsh mother, both in medical administration
Apprenticed to a body artist in the Ferment Quarter; the relationship lasted four years and ended badly — he does not discuss the details
Opens Meridian Flesh; initially struggling, reputation builds over three years
Begins noticing patterns in client complications linked to a specific Helix product line; starts keeping private records
Begins collaboration with Helix Biosystems on geneware integration techniques; finds himself in a conflict of interest he hasn't resolved

physical_description.heritage: Eurasian blend with Eastern European dominance (58.6%) tempered by Hispanic/Latin American (26.3%) and East Asian (15.1%) ancestry — creating a warm medium-brown complexion with golden undertones, Slavic angular bone structure softened by subtle East Asian eye geometry, and a substantial build reflecting the distributed genetics of his diverse heritage
physical_description.build: Large-framed and broad-shouldered with substantial muscle mass carried without aggression; deliberate in movement, economical in gesture. The weight is distributed across a solid foundation — not fat, not bodybuilder-sculpted, but the build of someone who has spent two decades standing at a workstation with precision tools
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with silver-gray threading throughout
physical_description.hair_style: Worn in locs, typically pinned up during work hours in a loose crown; worn loose and falling to shoulders in off-hours
physical_description.hair_length: Medium to Long (pinned and loose respectively)
physical_description.eye_color: Photochromatic iris modification — deep violet in normal light, darkening to near-black in bright light; modification was integrated at the sclera level with subtle luminescence at the edges of the iris during transition
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with subtle golden undertones; even pigmentation with age-appropriate weathering reflecting the balanced blend of Eastern European, Hispanic/Latin American, and East Asian ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Clean-shaven or very close-cropped facial hair; no visible scarring on the face; the skin shows the even tone of someone who takes care of it and who spends controlled hours indoors under studio lighting. Angular Slavic cheekbones and defined jawline with subtle monolid characteristics and soft eye-shape geometry from East Asian ancestry. His expression defaults to calm attentiveness — the resting face of someone listening
distinguishing_marks: Both forearms and upper arms are extensively tattooed in overlapping designs spanning twenty years of his own work — a living portfolio of evolving style with deliberate palimpsest layering where newer pieces integrate with and reference older work beneath them

Bioluminescent gene-mod design running the length of his spine beneath the skin — a trail of symbols in a script of his own invention, visible as subtle tracery under the skin in daylight and fully luminescent (soft blue-white) only in complete darkness
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The photochromatic iris modification is immediately visible and distinctive — the deep violet color and the subtle luminescence during light-transition are striking and clearly intentional. The extensive tattoo work across both arms reads as professional body art rather than augmentation, but the craftsmanship is evident. The spine modification is invisible in normal conditions; only visible in darkness or in medical imaging
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate slowness and precision — a conscious choice to avoid the threat-response that large men moving quickly can trigger. His posture is upright and open, shoulders relaxed. When working, he enters a state of focused stillness, hands moving with surgical precision while the rest of his body remains stable. In conversation, he makes direct eye contact and lets silences sit without filling them
physical_description.clothing_style: Studio uniform consists of fitted dark clothing (black or dark gray) that doesn't show pigment transfer from his work — typically well-tailored technical trousers and a long-sleeve compression shirt or fitted henley that displays his tattoo work on the forearms and upper arms. Over this, he wears a custom lab coat in matte black or dark charcoal with reinforced cuffs and an internal array of tool pockets; the coat fits him precisely and is clearly tailored for someone his size. Outside the studio, he wears similar colors and fits — quality technical fabrics, Tier 3 sustainable brands (Refugium, Reweave collective), no logos or corporate affiliation. His jewelry is minimal: a wedding band in dark platinum, and occasionally a single silver ring on his right index finger that he removes during client work. His locs are typically secured with silver or dark metal cuffs when pinned. There is no aspect of his appearance that reads as ostentatious, but everything reads as chosen and maintained with intention
